findings.title: Dynamic imports run eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazily loaded
findings.body:
Each property is assigned `import("./x")`, and that call runs immediately when the `appStore` object literal is evaluated. Importing `@calcom/app-store` (which `getCalendar`, `videoClient`, the payment helpers and others do) therefore starts loading all 28 app modules at once, just as the old static imports did.

The PR's goal of async/lazy loading is not met. Cold start and memory cost are unchanged, and every call site now pays an extra `await`.

There is also a new failure mode. If any app module throws during evaluation (for example a missing env var at import time), its promise rejects with no handler attached until some caller awaits that key. That produces an `unhandledRejection` at startup even for apps that are never used.

Fix: store thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call them at the use sites (`await appStore[key]?.()`).

findings.title: async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves rejections unhandled
findings.body:
The callback was changed to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })`. `forEach` ignores the returned promises.

Before this change, a synchronous failure in `getCalendar` (for example a `CalendarService` constructor throwing on a bad or undecryptable key) was caught by the enclosing `try { ... } catch` at lines 124-139 and logged.

Now every failure from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection that the try/catch can never see. Under Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` that can take down the process; at best the error is lost. The calendar/video deletions also run detached from `Reschedule`'s control flow.

Use `await Promise.allSettled(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (or a `for...of` with `await`) inside the try block.

findings.title: async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves rejections unhandled
findings.body:
This file has the same change as the vital app: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...) ... })`. `forEach` discards the promises.

Errors from `getCalendar` were previously thrown synchronously and caught by the try/catch at lines 124-139. They now become unhandled rejections that bypass the catch entirely. This can crash the process under Node's default unhandled-rejection mode, or the errors are silently lost. The deletions are also no longer tied to the function's execution.

Replace it with `await Promise.allSettled(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

findings.title: requestReschedule now fires calendar deletions as detached async callbacks with unhandled rejections
findings.body:
`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` produces promises that nobody awaits or catches.

Previously a failure in `getCalendar` would throw synchronously and surface as a mutation error. Now any `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection, while the mutation continues sending emails and webhooks as if the deletes had succeeded.

Collect the promises with `map` and `await Promise.allSettled(...)`, logging any failures.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials creates getCalendar promises that are discarded for non-calendar variants
findings.body:
`getCalendar(credential)` is now async and is called for every credential before the `app.variant === "calendar"` check. For apps whose type ends in `_calendar` but whose variant is not `"calendar"`, the returned promise is thrown away. If it rejects (for example a `CalendarService` constructor failing to decrypt a key), the rejection is never handled.

The returned `calendar` field also changes from `Calendar | null` to `Promise<Calendar | null>`. Every consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` must now await it, which is a silent contract change for callers other than `getConnectedCalendars`.

Only call `getCalendar` inside the `variant === "calendar"` branch.
